rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the disclosure quantitatively. Mode B: assess whether the trajectory (2023: top-3 = 44%; 2024 + 2025: top-2 = 40%) reflects customer consolidation risk that materially elevates earnings sensitivity to a single retailer's purchase decision.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Top-2 customers = 40% of FY2025 net sales = ~$852M of $2.13B revenue concentrated in two retailers (industry-known to be AutoZone, O'Reilly, Advance Auto, Genuine Parts — DORM does not name them but cohort analysis is unambiguous). No customer named per industry convention.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is honest but the concentration itself is structurally fragile. A single retailer destocking decision (which is exactly what happens when retailers face their own tariff-pass-through limits) materially moves DORM's quarterly revenue. The Q1 2026 10-Q's commentary that 'sales generally declined starting in the second half of 2025 and through the first quarter of 2026' is consistent with retailer destocking — although DORM attributes the $21M Q1 revenue rise to 'tariff-related pricing actions' with 'lower volume.' Volume is declining; only price is up. Once retailers refuse further price-through, the concentration risk materializes.

rfm_tuples.R: "Goodwill impairment charge represents a non-cash charge recorded in the year ended December 31, 2025, for the Heavy Duty reporting unit. As part of our annual goodwill impairment evaluation during the fourth quarter, management concluded that the carrying value of the Heavy Duty reporting unit exceeded its fair value and therefore recorded an impairment charge of $56.7 million, representing the goodwill balance in the Heavy Duty reporting unit as of the measurement date."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: a 100% goodwill writedown of an entire reporting unit is a strong managerial-pessimism signal. Cross-check segment income/margin trend and whether Heavy Duty was disclosed as 'temporary weakness' previously.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Heavy Duty segment: FY2025 net sales $232.6M (+0.5% YoY = essentially flat) with margin DOWN 60bps. The 10-K writes off the ENTIRE $56.7M Heavy Duty goodwill — implying management's DCF for that reporting unit no longer supports any premium over net assets. The 'freight transportation and trucking aftermarket pressures' DORM cites is consistent with the broader trucking cycle, but a 100% goodwill writedown is management telling you they have lost faith. Carve-out / divestiture risk is real but undisclosed.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 14 (Subsequent Events): "On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ('IEEPA') does not authorize the President of the U.S. to impose tariffs ... Although the Supreme Court ruling may allow importers to claim refunds of such previously paid IEEPA-related duties, no refund mechanism has been established ... No asset or gain related to potential tariff refunds has been recognized due to uncertainty regarding eligibility, amount, and timing." Q1 10-Q updates: "In March 2026, the Court of International Trade ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection ('CBP') to begin the refund process for all importers who were subject to IEEPA duties. CIT's order may be subject to U.S. government challenge. We are the importer of record for certain products that were previously subject to tariffs under IEEPA. While we intend to pursue refunds for IEEPA tariffs, there can be no assurance that we will receive all or any portion of such refunds. No adjustments have been recorded ..."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: assess the asymmetry. DORM previously expensed IEEPA tariff costs (~38% of purchases from China). If a refund is granted, it would be a one-time positive that is NOT in current numbers. Conversely, the new Section 122 tariffs (announced same day) put the run-rate margin at risk. The market is reasonably discounting tariff uncertainty.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 14 + Q1 2026 10-Q Impact of Tariffs)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Tariff-cost exposure: 77% of total purchase volume sourced non-U.S., ~38% from China. Q1 2026 gross margin compressed 490bps to 36.0% (vs 40.9% Q1 2025) — driven entirely by tariff-cost recognition LAGGING the prior-period price-through benefit (10-K narrative: 'we experienced an increase in gross margin in the second half of 2025 due to the timing of price actions taking effect before the higher tariff costs were recognized'). Q1 2026 income from operations dropped 26.6% YoY ($58.8M vs $80.1M). Section 122 temporary tariffs announced 2026-02-20 took effect 2026-02-24 — i.e., new tariffs replaced the invalidated IEEPA tariffs. The IEEPA refund opportunity is real (DORM is importer of record) but unquantified and subject to U.S. government challenge. The refund process is an off-balance-sheet asymmetric upside that the issuer correctly does not book.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B asymmetric optionality: a successful refund claim could be a 9-figure cash recovery (DORM paid IEEPA duties on ~$1.6B of annual import costs across 2025); if Section 122 replaces them at a similar rate, run-rate margin remains pressured. The disclosure is honest and appropriately conservative (no booking). This is a wildcard, not an underdelivery. Rated UNVERIFIABLE because the outcome depends on a future government action that cannot be assessed pre-cutoff.

The unit economics of the aftermarket parts business are deteriorating, and the company's hand-waving around 'pricing actions partially offset by lower volume' obscures how aggressively margins have rolled. Not RED_FLAG (transparent enough), but a clear MODERATE underdelivery vs the strategic narrative.

summary: DORM is a -29% drawdown name where the Form-4 forensic tape DELIVERS the canonical 'absence of expected buying' signal. Across 21 Form 4 filings and 3 Form 3s covering the entire pre-cutoff window, ZERO insider open-market code-P purchases by ANY officer or director, including a freshly-hired CFO-Designate (Rayfield, 2026-01-19) who had three months of single-digit-discount price action to deploy personal capital and did not. The only OPEN-MARKET transactions are code-S SALES by SVP/CIO Donna Long ($197K total at $103-124). Chairman Steven Berman's family block declined from 15% to 13% of shares outstanding via charitable gifting, not opportunistic adds. Meanwhile the company spent $77M on buybacks at avg ~$121 in Q4 2025 + Q1 2026 — i.e., shareholder cash deployed while insiders refused to commit personal cash. Business is honestly disclosed: $56.7M Heavy Duty goodwill writedown (100% of segment goodwill), Q1 gross margin -490bps to 36.0% from tariff cost recognition, 40% customer concentration (top-2 retailers), 77% non-U.S. supplier exposure with 38% China. IEEPA refund process is an unquantified positive optionality but Section 122 replacement tariffs offset. Balance sheet is clean (net leverage ~1.2x, no revolver draw, Oct 2027 maturity). The insider-vs-narrative gap is unambiguous: management's buyback authority says 'buy', their personal Form 4 ledger says 'no'. Verdict: SHORT-tier. The Form-4 evidence is among the most directional in the universe — 2 RED_FLAG findings with a clean balance sheet means the issue is durable underearning, not solvency. Severity: 2 PASS / 4 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 2 RED_FLAG / 1 UNVERIFIABLE.
